{{Quote|Recently, he has made an all-too-common Anx mistake that no slaver can afford to make: falling in love with a piece of his property. The chiliox-fruit of his eye is the beautiful Twi'lek slave Shakka, whom Kelvyyn has taken to having on his arm at social gatherings.|Tem Eliss on Graxol Kelvyyn's love of Shakka|<ref name="Gamer 7">{{GamerCite|7|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Anx}}</ref>}}
'''Shakka''' was a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] who was [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by [[Graxol Kelvyyn/Legends|Graxol Kelvyyn]], an [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] who had fallen in love with her. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the two attended the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] on the planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], viewing the [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]] from their friend [[Watto/Legends|Watto's]] [[Watto's box/Legends|viewing box]]. Shakka and Kelvyyn were later mentioned in [[sentientologist]] [[Tem Eliss|Tem Eliss's]] [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]''.

==Biography==
{{Quote|''Ten wupiupi'' says ''Sebulba'' will set a ''new speed record'' when he wins today.''&raquo;<br />&laquo;''Make it ''fifteen wupiupi'', and you have a ''bet!''|Watto and Graxol Kelvyyn bet in Shakka's company|<ref name="PodracingTales" />|translated=1}}
Shakka was a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Gender/Legends|female]]<ref name="DB" /> dancer<ref name="Insider 131">{{InsiderCite|131|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: An Audience of Aliens}}</ref> [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to<ref name="DB" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]].<ref name="DB" /> The dancer was [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] by [[Graxol Kelvyyn/Legends|Graxol Kelvyyn]], an [[Anx/Legends|Anx]] trader of enslaved beings based on her homeworld,<ref name="Gamer 7" /> and often attended events with him.<ref name="ActionFigure" /> Though Shakka was viewed as his property, Kelvyyn had fallen in love with<ref name="Gamer 7" /> her,<ref name="ActionFigure" /> frequently having the dancer on his [[Limb/Legends|arm]] at social gatherings.<ref name="Gamer 7">{{GamerCite|7|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Anx}}</ref> On the Outer Rim planet [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]],<ref name="CL" /> she and her enslaver were favorite locals<ref name="Hasbro" /> of the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]],<ref name="CL">''[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|Star Wars: Complete Locations]]''</ref> where their friend, the [[Toydarian/Legends|Toydarian]] [[Junk dealer/Legends|junk dealer]] [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], operated.<ref name="Kids15 (1999)" />

[[File:Wattos box.jpg|thumb|right|400px|Shakka and Graxol Kelvyyn (middle) visited Watto's box.]]
In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]</ref> the two visited Tatooine, where they attended [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|that year's]] [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]]. Shakka sat on the floor next to Kelvyyn<ref name="Phantom menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> inside [[Watto's box/Legends|a private viewing box]] used by Watto, located in the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena/Legends|Mos Espa Grand Arena]].<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|packtype=Cinema Scenes|pack=Watto's Box|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/episodeicswattosbox.asp}}</ref> After the [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|racer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]] made record [[Time/Legends|time]], Shakka smiled as Kelvyyn made [[Currency/Legends|bets]] with Watto.<ref name="PodracingTales">"[[Podracing Tales]]"</ref> The junk dealer's enslaved worker [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]],<ref name="Phantom menace" /> whom Shakka watched anxiously during the race,<ref name="Hasbro" /> eventually won.<ref name="Phantom menace" /> 

During the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="GalaxyGuide12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> the Twi'lek was mentioned alongside Kelvyyn in a [[Book/Legends|book]] titled ''[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life]]''.<ref name="Gamer 7" /> [[Iyra]] author and [[sentientologist]]<ref name="GalaxyGuide12" /> [[Tem Eliss]] wrote about the pair in a section on the Anx species.<ref name="Gamer 7" />

==Personality and traits==
Shakka, a [[Lethan/Legends|Lethan]] Twi'lek, had [[Color/Legends|red]] skin<ref name="Twi'lek" /> and brown [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="DB" /> She had a name of Twi'lek origin that translated to "[[Lightning (phenomenon)/Legends|lightning]]."<ref name="GalacticCampaign">''[[Galactic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Tem Eliss described her as beautiful<ref name="Gamer 7" /> and others considered the Twi'lek to be attractive.<ref name="ActionFigure" /> Her enslaver made the common Anx mistake of falling in love with something he viewed as property, taking to having Shakka on his arm during social gatherings. Eliss chronicled Kelvyyn's feelings for Shakka as her being the [[Chiliox tree|chiliox-fruit]] of his eye.<ref name="Gamer 7" /> The woman was friends with Watto and he enjoyed her and Kelvyyn's company when watching podracing.<ref name="Kids15 (1999)">{{Kids1999Cite|15|Meet Watto!}}</ref>

==Equipment==
During the podrace, Shakka wore a [[Clothing/Legends|bikini]] decorated with silver chains and beads, silver bottoms, a silver and white headdress, and a black spiky choker with chains attached to it. The Twi'lek also wore black spiky armbands below their shoulders and black strapped sandals.<ref name="Hasbro" /> The ensemble was property of Kelvyyn.<ref name="Wardrobe">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/fun/snapshot/2001/03/snapshot20010327.html|series=Episode I Snapshot|text=Shakka's rather abbreviated wardrobe}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Shakka first appeared, portrayed by an uncredited extra, in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="Phantom menace" /> released on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="Year">''[[Star Wars Year by Year: A Visual Chronicle]]''</ref> The character's scenes were shot at [[Leavesden Studios]],<ref name="Filming">{{InsiderCite|39|When Artoo Met Wicket}}</ref> near [[Wikipedia:London|London]].<ref name="Location">{{SWArchive|url=episode-i/bts/production/news19970929.html|text=First Phase Of Episode I Production Wraps At Leavesden Studios}}</ref> Before the film's release, on [[May 3]] of that year,<ref name="Collector">{{CollectorCite|6|Around the Galaxy}}</ref> Shakka was first pictured on a card released by collectable company [[Topps]] in their first series of [[1999 Topps Star Wars: Episode I Widevision Series 1|Star Wars: Episode I Widevision]] cards.<ref name="Intergalactic">{{Topps|set=1999 Topps Star Wars: Episode I Widevision Series 1|cardname=47 - Intergalactic Spectators|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/73014/cid/5263457/1999-Topps-Widevision-Star-Wars:-Episode-I-47-Intergalactic-Spectators}}</ref> Shakka was later identified in 1999 with the release of the "Watto's Box" Cinema Scenes set, part of toy company [[Hasbro|Hasbro's]] [[Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|Episode I]] toy line.<ref name="Hasbro" /> 

The [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|adaptation]] of Episode I, released by [[LucasArts]]<ref name="video game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> on [[May 18]], 1999,<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/1999/05/18/star-wars-hits-the-shelves|text=Star Wars Hits The Shelves|author=IGN Staff|date=1999-05-18|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20121121210047}}</ref> includes the Watto's box scene. However, Shakka is omitted from the adaptation.<ref name="video game" /> Additionally, the character's entry in the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] incorrectly described her skin as orange colored.<ref name="DB" />
